# Dust

A small command-line tool to quickly see which directories and files are using the most disk space.

Demo:

![Example](media/snap.png)

Overview

Dust prints a compact view of the biggest subdirectories or files. It automatically recurses into large subtrees so you can quickly find the biggest consumers of disk space. The display uses bars and colors to indicate relative usage and which parent folders subfolders belong to.

Usage

```
Usage: dust
Usage: dust <dir>
Usage: dust <dir> <another_dir> <and_more>
Usage: dust -p  (full-path - Show fullpath of the subdirectories)
Usage: dust -s  (apparent-size - shows the length of the file as opposed to the amount of disk space it uses)
Usage: dust -n 30  (Shows 30 directories instead of the default [default is terminal height])
Usage: dust -d 3  (Shows 3 levels of subdirectories)
Usage: dust -D (Show only directories)
Usage: dust -F (Show only files - finds your largest files)
Usage: dust -r (reverse order of output)
Usage: dust -o si/b/kb/kib/mb/mib/gb/gib (output format)
Usage: dust -X ignore  (ignore all files and directories with the name 'ignore')
Usage: dust -x (Only show directories on the same filesystem)
Usage: dust -b (Do not show percentages or draw ASCII bars)
Usage: dust -B (--bars-on-right - Percent bars moved to right side of screen)
Usage: dust -i (Do not show hidden files)
Usage: dust -c (No colors [monochrome])
Usage: dust -C (Force colors)
Usage: dust -f (Count files instead of diskspace)
Usage: dust -t (Group by filetype)
Usage: dust -z 10M (min-size, Only include files larger than 10M)
Usage: dust -e regex (Only include files matching this regex)
Usage: dust -v regex (Exclude files matching this regex)
Usage: dust -L (dereference-links - Treat symlinks as directories)
Usage: dust -P (Disable the progress indicator)
Usage: dust -R (For screen readers. Removes bars/symbols. Adds new column: depth level.)
Usage: dust -S (Custom Stack size)
Usage: dust --skip-total (No total row will be displayed)
Usage: dust -j (Prints JSON representation of directories)
Usage: dust --files0-from=FILE (Read NUL-terminated file paths from FILE)
Usage: dust --files-from=FILE (Read newline-terminated file paths from FILE)
Usage: dust --collapse=node-modules (Keep node_modules collapsed in display)
```

Config

Dust can read configuration from `~/.config/dust/config.toml` or `~/.dust.toml` to set default options.

Alternatives

- NCDU
- dutree
- dua
- pdu
- dirstat-rs

import os, subprocess, pathlib, shutil, sys
base=pathlib.Path("/tmp/fix1")
if base.exists(): shutil.rmtree(base)
base.mkdir()
# create structure
def write(p, size):
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_bytes(b"x"*size)
write(base/"a/big.bin", 20000)
write(base/"a/small.txt", 100)
write(base/"b/medium.bin", 5000)
write(base/"top.txt", 1000)
(base/"empty").mkdir()
os.symlink("a/big.bin", base/"linkfile")
os.symlink("a", base/"linkdir")
os.symlink("nonexist", base/"broken")
# hidden
write(base/".hidden/file", 3000)
write(base/".hiddenfile", 2000)

def run(args, cwd="/tmp", env=None, term_width=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    # ensure no config interference: HOME to empty
    e["HOME"]="/tmp/home_empty"
    os.makedirs("/tmp/home_empty", exist_ok=True)
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, env=e)
    return p

for args in [
 ["/tmp/fix1"],
 ["-P","-c","/tmp/fix1"],
 ["-P","-c","-b","/tmp/fix1"],
 ["-P","-c","-r","/tmp/fix1"],
 ["-P","-c","-p","/tmp/fix1"],
 ["-P","-c","-s","/tmp/fix1"],
 ["-P","-c","-s","-b","/tmp/fix1"],
]:
    p=run(args)
    print("ARGS",args,"rc",p.returncode)
    print(p.stdout, end='')
    print("STDERR:",repr(p.stderr))
    print("---")

    if r:
        chunk=os.read(p.stderr.fileno(),4096)
        if chunk:
            print(f"{time.time()-start:.2f}", repr(chunk))
            data+=chunk
    if time.time()-start>10:
        p.kill(); break
print("done", p.wait(), "stdout len", len(p.stdout.read()))

import subprocess, os, pathlib, shutil
base=pathlib.Path("/tmp/fixls")
if base.exists(): shutil.rmtree(base)
base.mkdir()
for name,mode in [("setuid",0o4755),("setgid",0o2755),("execsticky",0o1755),("normal",0o755)]:
    p=base/name; p.write_bytes(b"x"); os.chmod(p,mode)
for name,mode in [("dirsticky",0o1777),("dirotherw",0o0777),("dirboth",0o0777),("dirplain",0o755)]:
    p=base/name; p.mkdir(); os.chmod(p,mode)
os.chmod(base/"dirboth",0o1777|0o002) # actually 1777 already other w
# hardlink
(base/"hard1").write_bytes(b"x"); os.link(base/"hard1",base/"hard2")
def run(extra):
    env=dict(os.environ, HOME="/tmp/home_empty"); env.update(extra)
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-P","-C","-s","-b",str(base)],capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)

    print("---")

[package]
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.85"
name = "clap"
version = "4.6.1"
build = false
include = [
    "build.rs",

]
autolib = false
autobins = false
autoexamples = false
autotests = false
autobenches = false
description = "A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = [
    "argument",
    "cli",
    "arg",
    "parser",
    "parse",
]
categories = ["command-line-interface"]
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/clap-rs/clap"
resolver = "2"

[package.metadata.docs.rs]
features = ["unstable-doc"]
rustdoc-args = ["--generate-link-to-definition"]

[package.metadata.playground]
features = ["unstable-doc"]

[package.metadata.release]
shared-version = true
tag-name = "v{{version}}"

[[package.metadata.release.pre-release-replacements]]
file = "CHANGELOG.md"

min = 1
